title: PostgreSQL database security evidence baseline
description: Declarative, read-only evidence requests for encryption, data protection, access security, and masking governance in customer-validated PostgreSQL environments.

controls.title: Review observed TLS session metadata
controls.objective: Collect TLS metadata for sessions visible to the PostgreSQL collector so an authorized reviewer can compare observed connections with the approved transport-security policy.

applicability.notes: Validate pg_stat_ssl availability and visibility for the exact PostgreSQL deployment and managed-service configuration.

limitations: The probe observes currently visible sessions and does not prove that TLS is enforced for every client, listener, replica, backup path, or future connection.
Cipher and protocol acceptability must be evaluated against the customer's current cryptographic standard.

remediation.guidance: Review server TLS settings, certificate lifecycle, client authentication rules, managed-service controls, connection pools, and rollback procedures before changing transport configuration.

controls.title: Review row-security metadata
controls.objective: Collect table-level row-security flags so an authorized reviewer can compare declared protection boundaries with the approved application authorization design.

applicability.notes: Row-level security is assessed only where the application security design requires it.

limitations: The probe does not collect policy expressions, application authorization logic, table sensitivity, role bypass paths, or query outcomes.
A table without row security is not automatically noncompliant because the approved design may use a different authorization boundary.

remediation.guidance: Confirm data classification and the application authorization design, review ownership and BYPASSRLS paths, test policy behavior with representative roles, and obtain change approval before enabling row security.

controls.title: Review role attribute metadata
controls.objective: Collect high-impact PostgreSQL role attributes so an authorized reviewer can identify candidates for ownership, lifecycle, and least-privilege analysis.

applicability.notes: Role names are security metadata and must be handled under the approved identity-data policy.

limitations: The probe does not collect role memberships, object privileges, ownership, usage history, authentication method, or external identity state.
A powerful role attribute requires business-context review and does not by itself establish unauthorized access.

remediation.guidance: Correlate role ownership, effective memberships, object grants, recent use, service dependencies, and emergency access before an authorized PostgreSQL administrator changes role attributes.

controls.title: Review masking governance evidence
controls.objective: Require approved evidence that non-production PostgreSQL data uses appropriate masking techniques and that privacy, referential integrity, and application utility were validated.

applicability.notes: No masking probe is approved in the current collector catalog, so evidence review remains manual.

manual_evidence_requirements: Approved masking policy and scoped data classification
Execution record from the authorized masking mechanism

limitations: This control does not execute masking, inspect raw values, or assume that dynamic masking is a native PostgreSQL capability.
Document presence alone does not establish masking effectiveness; an authorized reviewer must evaluate the evidence.

remediation.guidance: Select an approved masking mechanism, define deterministic behavior where relationships require it, authorize execution, validate re-identification risk and application utility, and attach signed evidence.
